title: Regional priority quarantine and stream-trim for hosted-gateway active-active failover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Implement an active-active failover mechanism on the hosted API edge that preserves streaming session continuity when possible, enforces SLO-driven routing decisions, and uses a "priority quarantine" to isolate lower-value traffic during regional degradations. This ticket covers design + prototype for: (1) regional priority quarantine (ephemeral proxying + limited KV-write window), (2) stream-trim checkpointing to enable truncated resume when full handoff is impossible, (3) SLO-aware admission + circuit breaker policy that ties token admission to realtime headroom, and (4) integrated telemetry and rollback guards for canary rollout. This is targeted at hosted API traffic (edge gateways) where sessions may be long-lived streaming websockets or chunked HTTP responses.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype that can quarantine lower-priority sessions in an alternate proxy tier without violating client contract for high-priority sessions
Stream-trim algorithm implemented that can checkpoint and resume streaming sessions with <=1% user-visible token loss in simulated failover tests
Admission controller enforces per-region token-level SLO budget and exposes circuit state via /v1/internal/edge-circuit API
Automated canary (5% traffic) demonstrates graceful degradation path and automatic rollback on SLO breach over 10m windows
Dashboard shows latency (P50/P95/P99), error-rate, token-denied-by-circuit, and quarantined-session-count with 1m granularity
design_notes: Core concepts: priority quarantine isolates traffic by customer tier + route label. High priority (enterprise+dedicated-mapped) never enters quarantine unless region catastrophic; mid/low priority can be redirected to quarantine proxies that accept requests but outbound to serving runtime is rate-limited and allowed to use ephemeral cache-only KV reads. Stream-trim: when an in-flight streaming session cannot be fully rehydrated in fallback region, we capture a short checkpoint (last n tokens + light context hash), inform client of a truncated resume token, and resume generation on fallback model variant with 'trimmed' prefix semantics. Tradeoffs: checkpointing increases memory and metadata write rate (KV lease churn), and trimming risks truncating user context—we mitigate with configurable 'grace tokens' and a policy to prefer model variant that tolerates prefix mismatch. Admission/circuit policy is token-aware (not just request count) because LLM cost scales with output tokens. Circuit uses smoothed token burn rate vs allocated token budget (SLO budgets computed from global SLOs and current regional headroom).
implementation_plan: Spike: simulate quarantine proxies and run synthetic streaming sessions against two-region cluster (done)
Build: implement edge admission controller and /v1/internal/edge-circuit endpoint (backend + small console hook)
Integrate: stream-trim checkpoint writer with KV lease extension and compact metadata format
Telemetry: add metrics and dashboard; expose circuit state in tracing and logs
Canary: deploy to us-west-2 and run 5% production traffic for 48h; monitor SLOs and rollback criteria
Hardening: add automated rollback on token-error-rate > 0.5% over 10m and runbook updates
telemetry_queries: edge.gateway.tokens_per_minute{region=*} by region — used to compute token headroom
edge.gateway.stream_trim.resume_rate — fraction of resumes that used trimmed checkpoint
risks: KV lease churn from checkpoint writes could increase latency for other metadata operations
Trimming user context may surface subtle quality regressions for downstream apps that assume full-history generation
Priority quarantine could be gamed if client applications change route labels; need authentication + route-label enforcement
Rollout could interact with Dedicated customers pinned to region; must ensure isolation and not route enterprise traffic into quarantine
comments: 2025-01-11 - Aisha: Triage notes — this ticket unblocks work from PMs wanting a bounded-experience fallback for stream users. Marked P1 due to customer impact potential.
2025-01-14 - Liam: Spike completed — simulated 2k concurrent streams, quarantine proxies held <5% additional latency for high-priority paths and trimmed-resume success 93% in noisy conditions.
2025-01-18 - Design review (PM + SRE): Agreed to make checkpoint writes best-effort with TTL and GC to limit KV pressure. PM requested a canary window and explicit rollback thresholds.
